mentions.name: embeddedgdbmcp
mentions.description: An AI debugger for embedded systems, implemented as an MCP server that lets Claude talk directly to GDB. Instead of manually decoding registers like CFSR, users ask natural-language questions such as "why did it crash?" and get concrete answers like the faulting line and function, including diagnosing deadlocks between RP2040 cores. Version 0.1.0 has shipped.
mentions.problem: Debugging microcontroller crashes means spending hours staring at cryptic registers and manually decoding values to figure out the cause.
mentions.audience: Embedded developers debugging microcontroller crashes who otherwise spend hours decoding cryptic registers.
mentions.source_excerpt:
So I built an MCP server that lets Claude talk directly to GDB.
Now instead of manually decoding CFSR registers, I just ask "why did it crash?" and get back "division by zero at line 142 in calculate_average()".
